target_customer: Brazilian e-commerce merchants, mostly small and medium stores on Tray and VTEX, moving to larger retailers
problem: Online shoppers abandon checkout because of long registration and payment forms, so merchants lose sales.
business_model: Small percentage fee on purchases made by already registered shoppers in the network, plus subscription for the AI sales assistant
product_category: E-commerce one-click headless checkout and AI cart recovery

founders.name: Mario Marcoccia
founders.background_notes: Employers and school are stated in the January 2022 Startupi article for both founders; the article does not say which employer belongs to which founder, so it is applied to both. YC page lists only Marcoccia.

founders.name: Rafael Gibelli
founders.background_notes: Led the checkout rebuild at LivUp, where the idea started (Startupi, 2022-01). Named co-founder by Startupi; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Bolt
competitors.what: One-click checkout network for US e-commerce, cited by the press as the similar solution
competitors.funding_then: 400M USD raised in October 2021 at a 6B USD valuation per Startupi

technical_complexity.rationale: Headless checkout with payment integrations and a shared shopper identity across stores, on top of platforms such as Tray and VTEX. Standard engineering with integration work.

defensibility.rationale: A network of registered shoppers makes checkout faster across stores, but it needs many merchants to matter, and platforms could ship native one-click checkout.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company raised a larger seed in 2023 and added an AI sales assistant.

market_need_then: Brazilian e-commerce grew during the pandemic and merchants lost sales at checkout. The founders claimed a checkout 52 percent faster and up to 44 percent higher conversion (company claims, Startupi 2022-01).

branding.domain_note: Company site is comprarapida.co, not a .com; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct Portuguese conversion messaging, with a money back ROI guarantee on the site

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive Portuguese name that says the benefit but is generic; press covers funding, not the brand.

pivots.to: Checkout plus AI sales assistant for WhatsApp cart recovery
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC description and site show the AI assistant added later

outcome_analysis: Compra Rápida launched in June 2021 from a checkout rebuild one founder led at LivUp, joined YC in W22, and raised R$ 4 million in January 2022 and R$ 18 million in June 2023. It lists named Brazilian retail brands as customers and added an AI assistant. It is active with 21 people, and the key risk is that platforms or payment players copy one-click checkout.
notes: Amounts are in Brazilian reais (R$ 4M in 2022-01, R$ 18M in 2023-06) so amount_usd is null. Aggregators (Seedtable 740K USD, VCBacked 3.6M total) are unverified and not recorded. Two outlets (Startupi, Revista Oeste) confirm the 2022 round and Startupi confirms 2023. Aggregator profiles claim Marcoccia co-founded Encontri; unverified. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
